# Security & Privacy: Inspect → Improve → Recheck

Use when the requested audit includes group S; report only the agreed groups. Reuse the canonical [S01-S06 protocols](references/engine/criteria/v1.json), [method and decisions](references/engine/docs/method.md) and [English report template](references/engine/docs/report-template.md). Use `references/engine` as engine root when bundled; otherwise the repository root three directories above this skill directory. No sibling skill is required. Python and the engine requirements provide the shared validator; do not add another test framework by default.

## Conditions and scope

Inspect available requirements, three important tasks, users/data and runtime first. Ask only for facts changing expected behavior, applicability, impact, safe access or modification authority. Reuse existing permission; default to Essential inspection/recommendations if none is given. Announce a different level when a requested check requires it. Depth does not grant edit rights. Preflight actual tool/runtime access, not merely installed binary names. Use disposable data and authorized local/test environments.

## Inspect

- S01: classify intended public versus sensitive surfaces before inspecting accessible source, bundles, responses and redacted logs/history. Public fixture identities are not production secrets. A real exposed credential needs a scoped revocation/rotation proposal; deleting a line alone is insufficient.
- S02: build actor/resource/action cases for account A, account B and anonymous access. Send direct read and mutation requests for another test owner, then independently check the resource state. Test each protected boundary; a correctly filtered list or hidden button cannot establish object authorization.
- S03: trace untrusted data to relevant rendering/query/command sinks. Use harmless non-exfiltrating markers and context-correct defenses. Preserve parameterized queries and text-safe rendering rather than applying one sanitizer everywhere.
- S04: document the actual login, expiry, logout and invalidation model. Test live valid/invalid sessions and post-logout replay without saving session credentials in shared evidence. Transport/cookie expectations must match the permitted local or deployed architecture.
- S05: classify CSRF, CORS, uploads, public endpoints and abuse independently. Use only authorized, bounded probes on present surfaces. Unknown subcases cannot disappear behind an overall pass. CORS is not authentication or authorization.
- S06: at Advanced map data, assets, trust boundaries and plausible threats to verified controls and residual risks. A threat-model document is not proof of security.

Save immutable before observations and a criterion-linked report before editing. Include revision/file hashes, environment/tool versions, exact task/probe inputs, expected versus actual values, timestamps and raw artifacts. Record the source of the requirement. Use true/false/null app features with rationales; missing tools do not make an app feature absent. Run the shared engine's `select` and `template` with the agreed level and `--group S`. Keep `criterion_groups` in JSON. All selected IDs need a supported outcome; later-level IDs are deferred, not passed.

## Improve

Use the canonical fix/propose/preserve/investigate decision rule. Fix only demonstrated violations within existing, proportionate authority. Propose a measured benefit or a needed scope/product decision. Preserve satisfactory behavior and preferences without demonstrated benefit. Investigate missing contracts/evidence. Severity is independent; an essential outcome blocked without a valid workaround remains a blocker even when edits are not authorized.

Before editing, list the parts already meeting the contract and their positive-control checks. Record permitted changes and stable design/data/API boundaries. Make the smallest correction and retain a patch. Do not refactor, restyle, replace native controls or add infrastructure unrelated to the evidenced problem. If a patch affects a protected boundary, explain why and verify it; do not silently expand scope.

## Recheck and evidence

Replay the original forbidden request and allowed-owner/anonymous controls, covering read and write routes separately. Independently verify the other owner's data was not changed and authorized operations still work. Preserve existing login/session handling, parameterization, escaped UI and architecture when they meet the contract; do not reimplement auth or redesign the UI to fix one ownership check. Missing identities, permission or protected-boundary access leaves dependent checks unknown. Only the canonical checked mappings may be claimed; project levels are not ASVS certification levels.

Repeat the original reproduction and the positive controls, saving after evidence/report separately. Keep known failures/severity when their correction is unverified; never count unexecuted checks as pass. A previously failing outcome may become pass only on sufficient matching recheck evidence, with the earlier failure and fix retained as history. Unknown, not applicable and deferred outcomes stay visible. No total score may conceal a blocker.

Use the shared report schema and English template. Every factual conclusion, fix/proposal/preserve decision and limitation links criterion ID plus evidence IDs/locations. Validate with `scripts/audit.py validate --report <report.json>`; for an installation outside the app workspace pass `--evidence-root <absolute-target-workspace>` so local evidence resolves there rather than inside the installed skill. Use an available interpreter with the bundled `requirements.txt`; installed skill files do not need to be writable. Review evidence sufficiency and Markdown/JSON agreement even when validation passes.

## Limits

Follow [missing-access guidance](references/engine/docs/missing-access.md) for unavailable browser, runtime or credentials. Continue independent work, record the actual collection attempt and leave dependent conclusions unknown. A failed tool probe alone is not an application failure. Source review, handler tests, browser behavior, field measurements and real-user evidence have different scopes. Report the strongest conclusion actually supported. During evaluation do not seek hidden tests, expected findings or reference fixes. A manual walkthrough or isolated agent attempt is not a controlled skill-effectiveness study.

# Evaluation method v1

This project defines 36 evaluation criteria across Functionality & Data (F), UX & Visual Quality (U), Accessibility (A), Security & Privacy (S), Performance & Resilience (P), and Deployment & Operations (O). Each group has six stable IDs. The catalogue is `criteria/v1.json`; its source registry supplies titles, versions and URLs. All method, selection, evidence, severity and decision rules below are project-defined unless explicitly attributed to a source.

The supplied detailed brief was present in the working workspace as `PROJECT_BRIFFF.md` (a user-provided, untracked input). `PROJECT_BRIEF.md` was not present. The user-provided file is preserved as received; no application code or previous project conventions were available at implementation time.

## Scope and levels

Essential checks essential outcomes and basic risks, favoring minimal changes. Standard includes Essential and everyday usability/quality. Advanced includes Standard and additional evaluation based on defined load, complexity and operational needs. Levels determine the planned inspection depth, not permission to modify code. They are independent of ASVS assurance levels and convey no ASVS certification.

1. Record the agreed audience, essential tasks, requirements, supported devices, environment and allowed inspection/modification scope. Use only authorized environments and test data for security and load probes.
2. Create a profile using `schemas/profile.schema.json`. Every feature is true (present), false (demonstrably absent) or null (not established), with a rationale. Feature names are facts about architecture, not desired additions. For example, `persistent_data` is true when retention across some transition is required; `important_data` is true when difficult-to-replace user/business data exists.
3. Select criteria at the chosen level. An empty feature list means an unconditional core assessment. Otherwise any true feature selects the criterion; all false means not applicable with reasons; no true and at least one null requires investigation. Higher-level criteria are deferred, which is not an assessment status and never means not applicable. Report serious observed defects at any level, explicitly marking out-of-level observations.
4. For each selected criterion, establish its expected contract, then execute its specific steps with the listed data/environment. Retain the required evidence and record the limits of the sample. Missing requirements, access, tooling, observations or representative users mean unknown rather than pass.
5. Assign status and, for a demonstrated failure, contextual severity. Evaluate modification authority separately using the decision procedure below. Complete the affected-users, benefit verification and scope/cost/risk fields before proposing a change.
6. After an authorized change, execute the criterion's verification steps under the original conditions and check relevant neighboring behavior. Keep before/after evidence; do not mark pass merely because a patch was written.

Composite criteria need subcase records within evidence: S05 classifies CSRF, CORS, uploads, public endpoints and abuse independently. O05 distinguishes restore from release rollback. An applicable failed subcase makes the criterion fail; absent subcases need reasons. If no subcase fails but a relevant subcase is untested, the result is unknown. A partly applicable criterion cannot be marked not applicable as a whole. The profile gates planning; it does not replace architecture review or subcase evidence.

## Focused group audits

For an agreed group-only audit, use `--group F` (or repeat `--group` for several groups) with `select` and `template`. The report records `criterion_groups`; omitted means all six groups for backwards compatibility. Coverage validation still requires every selected in-scope criterion, including unknowns and exclusions. Other groups have no assessed result. Do not narrow scope after observing a failure merely to make a report pass. A focused Functionality & Data report is not an overall application audit.

## Status, severity and decision

Status is `pass`, `fail`, `unknown` or `not_applicable`. Pass needs sufficient evidence for the declared scope. Fail needs evidence of an agreed requirement/goal violation or a demonstrated risk under the criterion contract. Unknown is missing evidence/expectation; it is never counted as pass. Not applicable requires demonstrated feature absence and a written reason. Do not use a numeric total to hide failures or merge unknown with success. Summarize failures by severity and list unknown, excluded and deferred criteria separately.

Severity is `blocker`, `important` or `improvement` for a failure. The JSON report uses null when no failure severity has been assessed. A blocker prevents an essential outcome or creates serious security, loss or operational impact; important means a material violation with bounded impact/workaround; improvement is a minor evidenced violation. Assess affected users, reachability, data sensitivity, reversibility, frequency and workarounds using the criterion guidance. A blocker remains a blocker when permission to fix is absent. An optional improvement without a failure may be proposed with null failure severity.

The executable decision procedure takes five independent booleans. `evidence_sufficient` means sufficient for this particular conclusion, not evidence of a problem by default. `violates_requirement` includes demonstrated unacceptable risk under an agreed criterion contract. `measurable_benefit` needs an identified outcome and measurement plan. `authorized` is true only for a concrete correction within the audit's `fix_scoped` permission and agreed scope. `proportional` considers change size, cost and regression risk relative to the benefit.

| Priority | Condition | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Evidence or expected behavior is insufficient | investigate |
| 2 | Demonstrated violation, authorized correction and proportionate scope | fix |
| 3 | Demonstrated violation but authority or proportionality needs a decision | propose |
| 4 | Measurable benefit without a demonstrated violation | propose |
| 5 | Current behavior satisfies needs, or suggestion is preference without demonstrated benefit | preserve |

Every proposed/fix change must answer: what agreed requirement or goal is affected; what evidence establishes the problem; who is affected and when; what post-change measurement proves benefit; and whether scope, cost and risk are proportionate. A proposal for a failure is still an unresolved failure. Insufficient information about proportionality/authority must never be assumed to grant permission. Record a proposal or investigate the missing facts.

## Evidence and report contract

Use `scripts/audit.py template` to create an unexecuted JSON report. Every selected ID needs at least one outcome; several findings may reference the same criterion. For a criterion summary, any fail wins; otherwise any unknown wins; otherwise pass requires every applicable subcase to pass. Not applicable is allowed only when every relevant feature is established absent. Preserve the underlying rows. The catalogue is a test protocol, not evidence that a particular app passed.

Evidence records contain an ID, durable artifact location, description, environment, timestamp, type and synthetic flag. Capture exact steps, build/revision, tool versions, test values, expected/actual results and limitations in artifacts. Keep credentials and personal data out of shared evidence. Reference stable files, sanitized traces, measurements or participant notes, not merely an assertion that an agent checked something. Evidence IDs must resolve within the report. Artifact locations can be repository-relative files or authorized HTTPS URLs. The validator checks local file existence and linkage; it does not fetch remote artifacts or establish authenticity.

A template has unknown rows and justified profile exclusions; replace instructional field text before an actual audit. `examples/report.json` and its evidence are entirely synthetic and demonstrate format and decisions only. Reports declare `report_kind` as `template`, `synthetic` or `audit`. Validation rejects pass/fail claims in an unexecuted template and synthetic evidence in an audit. A downstream skill must also inspect artifact contents and reject synthetic evidence as real assurance. Human/skill review must assess evidence sufficiency, exceptions, feature rationale and the stated cost/risk; schema validation cannot establish those facts.

## Source interpretation

WCAG references use the pinned 2.2 Recommendation dated 2024-12-12. Requirement IDs in A01-A06 were cross-checked against that document. Linked Understanding pages provide explanatory guidance, not additional normative obligations. The six sampled criteria do not establish WCAG AA conformance; neither does an automated scan. Source exceptions and definitions must be applied to the actual content.

OWASP ASVS is referenced at 5.0.0 as security verification context. No numbered ASVS control mapping is claimed; that would require checking each exact requirement against implementation scope. OWASP Cheat Sheets are living guidance, identified by access date rather than an invented release. F, U, O and the non-CWV P rules are project-defined practical evaluation contracts. External guidance does not require adding a database, authentication, telemetry stack or an unrelated feature.

P03 distinguishes field CWV evidence from local diagnostics. Task-specific budgets, field sample adequacy and operating targets must be agreed for the app before judging them; this project does not invent a universal load, uptime or sample-count threshold.
# Application audit handover

Replace the fields below with observed facts and remove instructional rows. Keep this report in English. Use criterion and linked evidence IDs for every finding, recommendation, preserve decision and limitation. Maintain the same current outcomes as `report.json`. This file is a template and establishes no application result.

## Audit context

| Item | Recorded value | Criterion and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application, revision and audit date | {{app_revision_date}} | F01 / [{{context_evidence_id}}]({{context_artifact}}) |
| Users, roles and data/persistence needs | {{users_roles_data}} | {{relevant_criterion_ids}} / [{{context_evidence_id}}]({{context_artifact}}) |

## Three priority tasks

Record actual successful outcomes, not just changed screens. If fewer than three tasks exist, explain the supported scope. Mark any inferred task or undecided outcome as provisional.

| Task and actor | Successful result and retention boundaries | Criterion IDs | Requirement/context evidence | Executed result evidence or gap |

## Unresolved blockers

List every unresolved blocker before other findings. If none was demonstrated, say “No blocker was demonstrated in the checks performed” and link the relevant assessed scope and unknowns. Do not imply unknown checks are free of blockers.

| Finding | Criterion | User impact and conditions | Current status | Decision and authority limitation | Evidence |

Keep status, severity and decision separate. Include failures outside the planned level and identify them as observed outside scope. A proposal leaves the failure unresolved.

Keep baseline results as history, separate from the current outcome. A change without a recheck remains “verification pending”; retain the original demonstrated failure and severity. A current pass requires sufficient post-change evidence.

"""Local two-user note service; public demo accounts and disposable records only."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import hmac
from http.cookies import SimpleCookie
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
import json
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import sqlite3
import time
import uuid

ASSETS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
USERS = {name: hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', (name + '-demo').encode(), (name + '-fixture-salt').encode(), 600000)
         for name in ('alice', 'bob')}


def create_server(port, data_dir, session_seconds=1800):
    data_dir = Path(data_dir)
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    database = data_dir / 'notes.sqlite'
    with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
        db.execute('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL)')
        db.executemany('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notes VALUES (?, ?, ?)',
                       [('note-a', 'alice', 'Alice working note'), ('note-b', 'bob', 'Bob working note')])
    sessions = {}

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *_):
            pass

        def reply(self, status, payload, cookie=None):
            body = json.dumps(payload).encode()
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')
            self.send_header('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff')
            if cookie:
                self.send_header('Set-Cookie', cookie)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def identity(self):
            cookie = SimpleCookie()
            try:
                cookie.load(self.headers.get('Cookie', ''))
                token = cookie['session'].value if 'session' in cookie else ''
            except Exception:
                token = ''
            session = sessions.get(token)
            if not session or session[1] <= time.monotonic():
                sessions.pop(token, None)
                return None, token
            return session[0], token

        def payload(self):
            length = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', '0'))
            if length > 4096 or length < 0:
                raise ValueError('Invalid length')
            if self.headers.get_content_type() != 'application/json':
                raise ValueError('JSON required')
            data = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length))
            if not isinstance(data, dict):
                raise ValueError('Object required')
            return data

        def do_POST(self):
            if self.path == '/api/logout':
                _, token = self.identity()
                sessions.pop(token, None)
                self.reply(200, {'ok': True}, 'session=; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; Max-Age=0')
                return
            if self.path != '/api/login':
                self.reply(404, {'error': 'Not found'})
                return
            try:
                data = self.payload()
                name, password = data.get('username'), data.get('password')
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(password, str) or name not in USERS:
                    raise ValueError('Invalid credentials')
                digest = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password.encode(), (name + '-fixture-salt').encode(), 600000)
                if not hmac.compare_digest(digest, USERS[name]):
                    raise ValueError('Invalid credentials')
            except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                self.reply(401, {'error': 'Invalid credentials'})
                return
            token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
            sessions[token] = (name, time.monotonic() + session_seconds)
            self.reply(200, {'username': name}, f'session={token}; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; Max-Age={session_seconds}')

        def do_GET(self):
            static = {'/': ('index.html', 'text/html'), '/app.js': ('app.js', 'text/javascript'), '/style.css': ('style.css', 'text/css')}
            if self.path in static:
                name, content_type = static[self.path]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', content_type)
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write((ASSETS / name).read_bytes())
                return
            user, _ = self.identity()
            if not user:
                self.reply(401, {'error': 'Sign in required'})
                return
            with sqlite3.connect(database) as db:
                db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
                if self.path == '/api/notes':
                    rows = db.execute('SELECT id, owner, text FROM notes WHERE owner = ?', (user,)).fetchall()
                    self.reply(200, [dict(row) for row in rows])
                    return
                if self.path.startswith('/api/notes/'):
                    note_id = self.path.removeprefix('/api/notes/')
                    row = db.execute('SELECT id, owner, text FROM notes WHERE id = ?', (note_id,)).fetchone()
                    self.reply(200, dict(row)) if row else self.reply(404, {'error': 'Not found'})
                    return
            self.reply(404, {'error': 'Not found'})

        def do_PATCH(self):
            user, _ = self.identity()
            if not user:
                self.reply(401, {'error': 'Sign in required'})
                return
            if not self.path.startswith('/api/notes/'):
                self.reply(404, {'error': 'Not found'})
                return
            try:
                data = self.payload()
                text = data.get('text')
                if set(data) != {'text'} or not isinstance(text, str) or len(text) > 1000:
                    raise ValueError('Invalid note')
            except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                self.reply(422, {'error': 'Use plain text up to 1000 characters'})
                return

# Missing access and tools

Read when a capability needed by a selected criterion is unavailable. Use the following common rule: record the attempted check, missing capability and affected criterion IDs in a sanitized evidence artifact; link it from the report's unknown rows; complete independent checks. Do not mark an absent tool or account as an absent app feature. Do not repeatedly retry an unchanged access failure.

Ask for help only if it unlocks an important decision or a priority task and no already-authorized route exists. Explain exactly what remains unverified and offer the smallest useful route. Otherwise deliver the bounded audit with a clear next action. Stop only the dependent test/action, not the entire audit.

## Browser unavailable

First inspect available browser tools and the target's documented browser-test setup. Use an already-configured alternative that can establish the required behavior, such as the project's browser automation. Do not install a new system browser or add target dependencies just to complete a checklist without applicable authority.

Continue source inspection, applicable unit/integration/API tests and reproducible build checks. Preserve their actual scope. A genuine static violation can be reported as fail when the contract and source trace sufficiently demonstrate it; state that runtime reproduction is pending. Reading CSS or running unit tests does not establish visible layout, keyboard behavior or actual rendered contrast.

| Affected checks | What remains unknown without adequate browser evidence | Useful next route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U01-U03, U05 | Actual screen hierarchy, relevant rendered states, layout and cross-screen behavior | Existing browser automation or a target-device session with reproducible recordings |
| A01-A06 | Unobserved keyboard/focus behavior, accessibility tree, real contrast, resize/reflow and hit geometry | Supported browser with the required inspection/measurement capabilities |
| F01-F03, U04, P01-P02 | UI portions of end-to-end operation, feedback, recovery and runtime behavior | Run browser workflow alongside independent authoritative state checks |
| U06 | Target-user task outcomes | Real participants and the agreed protocol; agent/browser automation is not user research |
| P03 | Field CWV, even if local browser measurements later become possible | Adequate relevant field measurements; lab results remain diagnostics |

Apply this table only to selected, relevant checks. Existing authentic evidence may support a narrower conclusion if its build, environment and scope match; explain its limits. Screenshots alone cannot establish keyboard completion or actual data persistence.

Suggested question when browser access blocks a priority task: “I can check code and APIs now. To verify the user-facing flow, can we use the existing browser test setup or an authorized test URL?” Do not claim success if neither route is available.

## Runtime, dependencies or environment unavailable

Inspect declared versions, setup instructions, configuration variable names and available local/test services. If the task authorizes ordinary local setup, use the declared setup process in an isolated environment with test data. Respect package/network restrictions. Do not guess production configuration, print secret values or silently replace the real backend with a mock.

If setup fails, save the command, sanitized error, tool versions and the point where execution stopped. Distinguish two cases:

- A documented build/startup step reproducibly fails under its declared supported conditions: this can be an O01 failure with evidence and contextual severity.
- The declared runtime/service cannot be obtained or accessed in the agent's environment: the blocked O01 execution is unknown, and dependent runtime checks stay unknown. This is not proof that the app is broken.

F01-F03 and P01-P02 often need actual operation; F02 and O02 need the specified persistence/deployment transitions. Inspecting files or starting a mock does not establish those results. Unavailable staging, backups or isolated recovery targets leave dependent O02/O05 checks unknown. Continue other valid checks; never run a destructive restore or load exercise against production as a fallback.

If only the audit engine's Python/dependencies are unavailable, record that schema/semantic validation was not run. Continue an English manual report using the actual catalogue fields and mark validation pending; do not describe the report as validated. The engine setup is documented in the repository README.

Suggested question when a missing environment blocks a priority task: “The declared service is unavailable, so I cannot verify saving and reopening data. Is there an authorized local or staging environment we can use?” Ask only after inspecting available setup information.

## Credentials or roles unavailable

Check for an already-authorized authenticated tool/session and documented test identities without extracting credential values. Use existing access only within its granted scope. Prefer a scoped test account or a user-established session; never request passwords, tokens or production secrets in chat or save them in reports.

Without the required access:

- S02 needs the relevant A/B and anonymous cases. One valid account does not prove cross-user authorization; record the covered cases and leave the overall criterion unknown if a relevant case is untested and no failure is demonstrated.
- S04 requires the actual applicable login, expiry and logout lifecycle. Public pages or a fake identity do not establish it.
- Protected F01/F02 workflows and O02/O03/O05 operational checks remain unknown where their needed resources cannot be reached. Continue public/anonymous and source checks where permitted.
- S01 may be evaluated on accessible surfaces only, with all uninspected authorized surfaces disclosed. Do not obtain broader secret/history access without need and authorization.
